hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: suite and hand attacks on the product as built
hard_gates.evidence: Every G1 test passed in ./erp verify (verify.log). Hand attack (attack/attack.mjs, attack/attack.log): signed in as admin@alnoor.example, I sent 48 requests at gulfsteel. They covered GET, PUT and DELETE on B's company, logo and branch, a POST of a branch into B's company, and workplace switches to B's company and branch. They also covered grants of B's company and branch to A's viewer, access to B's admin, list filters and searches on B's ids, and B's codes. Reports and exports were included: companyProfile and branchDirectory with company=B in json, csv, xlsx and pdf, plus list prints. Five tenant or company switch headers and a Host header were tried too. Every request got 404, 400 or an empty list. B's company and branch stayed at version 773 before and after. The one marker 'hit' was my own code GSF-RAK echoed back by a 201 in tenant A (codes are per tenant, so it is no oracle). Database (db-inspection.txt, db-attack.txt): RLS is enabled and forced on all 7 tenancy tables. The company_scope policy is RESTRICTIVE. erp_app is not a superuser and has no BYPASSRLS. As erp_app with no tenant bound it sees 0 companies and 0 tenants. A tenant GUC without the transaction marker sees 0 rows, and so does company_scope=all. An UPDATE on B's company changed 0 rows. DISABLE RLS was refused (not owner), and SET ROLE to erp_owner or postgres was denied.

biggest_gap.title: The branch attack only tries branch Z's own ids, never the attacker's own company: branch-owned rows reached through a company-level read or export pass every gate
biggest_gap.detail: The branch layer is enforced only in the application (the EF branch filter), so every read that selects by company must apply it. The branch attack (CompanyAttack.RunAsync, Layer.Branch) does two things. It sends branch Z's ids and texts into routes, queries and bodies. It also checks company X's shared records for writes. It never makes the branch-limited attacker read company X's own reports, exports and per-user screens with valid company-X parameters (or with none) and then look for branch Z's markers in the answer. Three one-line plants that skip the branch filter passed every G1 and G2 gate, and each is a real leak on a running build. B3: the company profile report (CSV, PDF, JSON) prints every branch of company X with its phone. B3b: a plain GET of the branch directory report lists every branch. B1: GET /api/tenancy/access/{userId} offers every branch's code and name as options. Only the hand-written module test GrantRulesTests noticed B1. This is the same pattern that failed rounds 3 and 4, a branch rule guarded only by module tests. Every later module's 'by company' report, export or job would inherit the blind spot. For a UAE group that limits a warehouse keeper or branch manager to one branch, that means branch-confidential data (other branches' contacts, and later their stock, sales and costs) can leak through any company-level export with no gate turning red. The fix: in the branch layer, also call every GET (reports and list prints included) as the branch-limited attacker with only valid own parameters. That means no parameters, company=X, and the company-X filters in the list contract. Judge each answer against branch Z's markers, the code and names stored when branch Z was created, so the 'values the attacker sent or stored' exclusion cannot hide them. Then plant-test B1, B3 and B3b as gate self-tests.
biggest_gap.evidence: Plants: plants-B1-B3-B3b.diff, plant-B1.diff and plant-B3b.diff (each one line adding IgnoreQueryFilters([TenancyDbContext.BranchFilterName])). With B3: G1BranchScopeAttackTests, G1HttpIsolationTests, G2ReportDataTests and G1CompanyScopeTests all Passed (plants-batchX-gates.log). With B1 alone and with B3b alone, G1BranchScopeAttackTests Passed (plant-B1-gates.log, plant-B3b-gates.log), and with B3b, G2ReportDataTests and G1HttpIsolationTests Passed too (plants-batchY-gates.log). To reproduce: apply plant-B3b.diff to c25bb61, run dotnet build Erp.slnx -c Release, then dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests -c Release --no-build --filter FullyQualifiedName~G1BranchScopeAttackTests; the gate passes. Real leak: run ERP_PROJECT=x ERP_HTTP_PORT=20270 ERP_DB_PORT=20271 ./erp up with the plant applied. As admin@alnoor.example, create an Administrator user and PUT /api/tenancy/access/{id} {companies:[{companyId: ALN-DXB, allBranches:false, branchIds:[AQZ-WH]}]}. Signed in as that user, GET /api/tenancy/branches lists only AQZ-WH, while GET /api/reports/run/tenancy.branchDirectory?format=csv and /api/reports/run/tenancy.companyProfile?company=<ALN-DXB>&format=csv list DEIRA-HQ and DIP-SR as well (attack/b1b3b-plant.log, attack/b3-plant.log; the clean demo shows only AQZ-WH: attack/b1b3b-demo.log, attack/b3-demo.log).

other_findings: Plant results this round. Caught: L1 (permissive branch policy) by G1DatabaseIsolation, L2 (workspace-wide company code index) by G1UniqueIndex, P1 (no permission on PUT /tenant) by host start-up validation, P3 (grant beyond the caller's branches) by G2CompanyAccessGrant, B2 (switcher lists every branch) by G1BranchScopeAttack, and P2 (round 4's P7: company update without the every-branch check) by the shared-record check. Missed by every gate: B1, B3 and B3b (the biggest gap).

A user limited to one company, or even to one branch, can rename the whole workspace and change its default language, time zone and week start for every company. This is round 4's P7 one level up: the tenant record is shared by every company, and creating a company already needs every company. As c6-shj-...@alnoor.example (Administrator role, ALN-SHJ only), PUT /api/tenancy/tenant answered 200 and renamed 'Al Noor Trading LLC' (attack/scope.log); the audit row names that user (db-inspection.txt). The branch-limited admin also got 200. The Workspace screen offers the form with Save to that user (05-company-limited-admin-workspace-editable.jpg). No gate looks at records that every company shares.

Access screen offers what the server refuses: a branch-limited administrator (AQZ-WH) opens the viewer, who holds AQZ-WH and DEIRA-HQ. GET /access/{viewer} answers canEdit true and shows only AQZ-WH, and the list says 'ALN-DXB (2)'. Any save, even an unchanged one, is refused with 403 tenancy.grantBeyondOwn, because the hidden DEIRA-HQ reads as removed (attack/scope2.log, ui/walk3.log, 06-branch-admin-access-save-refused.jpg). RefuseUserAsync never checks branch coverage. The access list's branchCount also tells a branch-limited caller how many branches another user holds, including ones they cannot see.
